units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Yes. What can a fellow do out of doors in this eternal rain? But I hear dinner is ready. That's capital!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: With a parcel, from the dining-room.
A parcel has come for you, Mrs. Alving.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Hands it to her.
With a glance at MR. MANDERS.
No doubt copies of the ode for to-morrow's ceremony.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: H'm--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: And dinner is ready.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Very well. We will come directly. I will just--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Begins to open the parcel.
To OSWALD.
Would Mr. Alving like red or white wine?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Both, if you please.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Bien . Very well, sir.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: She goes into the dining-room.
I may as well help to uncork it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: He also goes into the dining room, the door of which swings half open behind him.
Who has opened the parcel.
Yes, I thought so. Here is the Ceremonial Ode, Pastor Manders.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: With folded hands.
With what countenance I am to deliver my discourse to-morrow--!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, you will get through it somehow.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Softly, so as not to be heard in the dining-room.
Yes; it would not do to provoke scandal.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Under her breath, but firmly.

No. But then this long, hateful comedy will be ended. From the day after to-morrow, I shall act in every way as though he who is dead had never lived in this house. There shall be no one here but my boy and his mother.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: From the dining-room comes the noise of a chair overturned, and at the same moment is heard:
Sharply, but in a whisper.
Oswald! take care! are you mad? Let me go!
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Starts in terror.
Ah--!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She stares wildly towards the half-open door.
OSWALD is heard laughing and humming.
A bottle is uncorked.
Agitated.
What can be the matter? What is it, Mrs. Alving?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Hoarsely.
Ghosts! The couple from the conservatory--risen again!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Is it possible! Regina--? Is she--?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes. Come. Not a word--!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She seizes PASTOR MANDERS by the arm, and walks unsteadily towards the dining-room.
The same room.
The mist still lies heavy over the landscape.
MANDERS and MRS. ALVING enter from the dining-room.
Still in the doorway.
Velbekomme
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Note: A phrase equivalent to the German Prosit die Mahlzeit --May good digestion wait on appetite.
, Mr. Manders.
units.name: MRS. ALVING
